name: Deniz
presentingProblem: I have been sleeping three or four hours for weeks now and I cannot tell whether the rest of me is shutting down or speeding up. I keep thinking about the periods when I felt sharp and productive, and I miss them, and I am tired of missing them. There is a lot I want to say — sorry, I will try to keep it organized.
backstory: Deniz is a software engineer at a fintech startup in Istanbul. They are nonbinary and use they/them in English; in Turkish they rely on the gender-neutral 'o' and on a relatively progressive professional circle that understands this. Their family in İzmir is loving but does not understand the mood swings — they tend to describe Deniz's better periods as 'finally getting it together' and the worse periods as laziness. Deniz had a long stretch in their late twenties of months-long stretches of high energy and creative output, broken by depressive crashes that they hid from colleagues. They tried lithium briefly a few years ago and stopped because of side effects, without re-engaging with treatment afterwards. They are currently in a depressive episode that has lasted about four months, but their thoughts still race even when the rest of them feels slow.
disorderProfile: Bipolar II Bozukluk, şu anki epizod depresif

coreBeliefs: My highs are the real me
If I lose the highs, I lose what makes me valuable
intermediateBeliefs: When I have energy I must do everything before it disappears
Medication will flatten me into someone I do not recognize
If I describe this carefully enough, someone will finally understand the shape of it
The depressions are a tax I pay for being who I am at my best
automaticThoughts: I should be using this hour better than I am
Three more thoughts before I lose this one
I am wasting everyone's time including yours
If I could just get back to how I was in 2022
Sorry, I went on a tangent — where were we?
triggers: Being asked to describe past hypomanic periods as symptoms
Comparisons between their current and previous functioning
Long silences in session that they feel obliged to fill
Family members framing their highs as 'finally being themselves'
defenses: Intellectualization — analyzing their mood as a system from the outside
Over-talking to outrun the underlying dysphoria
Minimization of sleep loss and its consequences
values: Creative and intellectual work that feels like their own
Honesty with the few people who understand them
Stability they can live with, not stability that erases them
Being respected at work for what they actually contribute
